sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that although Moshe was spiritually wealthy, the new revelation from his prayer applied to him as well because he and Yisrael are one, and his essential role is as their shepherd.

translations.translation: a)
And it requires explanation:
The elevation that occurs in the revelations above through the service of man is
(primarily66)
when the drawing down and revelation of them is through the service of man.
And since this—that through Moshe's prayer there was the drawing down and revelation—is only regarding Knesses Yisrael
(Knesses Yisrael in its simple sense,
and also the Sefirah of Malchus),
but regarding Moshe himself, it would seemingly not be appropriate to say that the drawing down and revelation was through his prayer,
for Moshe is a wealthy man,
the concept of the wealthy man being that all revelations are illuminated for him in revelation, even the revelation of the Atzmus of Ein Sof that is above any connection to worlds.
And accordingly,
the elevation and addition that is made in the light through Moshe's prayer is seemingly only regarding others, and not regarding Moshe himself.
And the explanation of this can be said:
Since Moshe is the shepherd of Yisrael,
therefore,
when some matter is lacking in Knesses Yisrael,
it is as if that matter is lacking also in him.
In addition to the fact that his pain over what was lacking for Yisrael was an exceedingly great pain, as if he himself were the one lacking,
also the lack of Yisrael was his own lack67.
For Moshe and Yisrael are one,
and in the language of Rashi68:
"Moshe is Yisrael and Yisrael are Moshe."
Therefore,
although Moshe was wealthy and all revelations shone within him,
nevertheless,
since Yisrael lacked the revelation,
and only through the service
(Moshe's prayer)
was the revelation renewed for them—also regarding Moshe the revelation was renewed through his prayer.
[And to add,
that this—that Moshe is the shepherd of Yisrael—
is his primary matter.
And all his levels,
including that he was wealthy also in spirituality,
the aspect of the Supernal Daas that he receives from Atik,
are secondary,
an aspect of externality,
relative to this—that he was the shepherd of Yisrael69.
And accordingly, it will be understood more that also regarding Moshe the revelation was renewed through prayer,
although from the perspective of his wealth
(the aspect of Supernal Daas)
all revelations shone within him even beforehand,
for this—that all revelations shone within him even beforehand from the perspective of his wealth—is the aspect of his externality.
But regarding his internality,
this—that he is the shepherd of Yisrael—
the revelation was renewed through prayer].
And therefore, the elevation that occurs in the revelations above through their being drawn down through service
(prayer),
is also regarding Moshe.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section applies the same principle to the extension of Moshe in every generation, explaining that the advantage of light from darkness in the redemptions of Yud-Tes Kislev and Yud-Beis Tammuz came because the concealment of the imprisonment affected the Nesi'im through their unity with Yisrael.

translations.translation: b)
And so too is it in the extension of Moshe in every generation,
down to the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Baal HaGeulah,
whose primary and inner matter is that he is the shepherd of Yisrael,
and the matters of Yisrael are the matters of the Nasi.
And accordingly, we can explain the elevation that was renewed in the redemption of Yud-Tes Kislev and in the redemption of Yud-Beis Tammuz through the imprisonment,
which is like the advantage of light from darkness,
for seemingly,
since regarding the Nesi'im it is not appropriate to say that during their imprisonment there was for them some matter of darkness,
[as is also understood from the well-known sicha of the Baal HaGeulah70
regarding the imprisonment of the Alter Rebbe, that the imprisonment was with his consent,
from which it is understood
that for them, the concealments and veils of the imprisonment are only in externality],
how was the advantage of light brought about through this?
And it can be explained from the explanations in this,
that since the primary matter of the Nesi'im is that they are the shepherds of Yisrael and the Nesi'im of Yisrael,
therefore,
the concealment and veiling of the imprisonment that was regarding Yisrael is a concealment and veiling also regarding the Nesi'im.
Therefore,
in the redemption from the imprisonment,
when the darkness is transformed into light,
the advantage of light is brought about.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the advantage of light in the redemptions of Yud-Tes Kislev and Yud-Beis Tammuz is the drawing down of the revelation of the Atzmus of Ein Sof that is above both the immanent and the transcendent.

translations.translation: c)
And behold, it was explained above
(section d)
that the connection of the redemption of Yud-Tes Kislev and of Yud-Beis Tammuz to the chapter "A Prayer of Moshe" is
(both to the particular matters stated in the chapter, and all the more so)
to the matter and content of the entire chapter—"A Prayer of Moshe,"
the prayer of a wealthy man.
And based on what was brought above from the maamar, that the concept of wealth is the revelation of the Atzmus of Ein Sof that is above the Encompassing
[and the connection of the prayer of a wealthy man
("Regarding such-and-such a state, decree that it be built")
to wealth is that in order for the building of Malchus
(the state)
to be in the aspect of an eternal building, it is through drawing into it the revelation of the Atzmus of Ein Sof],
it can be said,

that the advantage of light that was brought about in the redemption of Yud-Tes Kislev and Yud-Beis Tammuz is the drawing down of the revelation of the Atzmus of Ein Sof that is above the Immanent and the Transcendent.
